body.purpose: Root size: filter text, notice copy, and button labels.

name.purpose: Link names, which wrap instead of truncating.

components.name: Top Bar

narrative.overview:
The familiar dashboard grid, played straight and sharpened. Links sit in square tiles sized to their content in justified rows instead of floating rounded cards, so the screen can be scanned at a glance. Nothing competes with the links: the only chrome above the grid is a thin top bar holding the title, a filter field, and a settings control.

The world is monochrome and quiet by construction. A pure white or deep slate ground, cool neutral ink, one typeface, zero radius, and low-alpha hairlines do all the structural work. Density is high and even, with every link given the same weight, because the visitor arrives knowing what they want. Color arrives from four places only: the logos themselves, small squares on configured labels, a single amber signal that marks where input is and what Enter will do, and red on a count of things that are down.

This system rejects sidebars, free-standing stat cards, hero headers, and soft shadows. It is a dashboard and does not pretend otherwise; the craft is in the precision of the grid rather than in a concept layered over it.
keyCharacteristics: Square tiles sized to their content, 8px apart, in justified rows that interlock vertically; equal lanes on phones
Neutral header strips with a small tracked uppercase group name and a tabular count
Zero radius on every surface and control
One amber accent, reserved for focus, top match, and selected settings
Light and dark themes defined as single paired tokens

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: In the interface, amber marks only where input is and what Enter will do: focus, caret, selection, top match, and selected setting. It never decorates and never signals hover.

rules.name: The Content Color Rule
rules.body: Hue beyond amber and Down Red comes only from configured content: bookmark icons, including monochrome icons given their own color, and the square on a label given a color. Chrome stays neutral, and text never takes a configured color, so contrast holds for any value.

rules.name: The Down Rule
rules.body: Red marks only a count of things that are down, and only above zero. A healthy dashboard shows no red, and a zero stays in faint ink.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Sans carries every role. Hierarchy comes from weight and small size steps, never a second face.

rules.name: The Real Structure Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase names real structure only: a group or a set of controls it directly labels. It never sits as a decorative line above other text.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes while filtering uses tabular numerals, so counts do not jitter.

rules.name: The Content Size Rule
rules.body: Inside a group, each tile is as wide and as tall as its content, 8px from its neighbours. Full rows stretch to both edges and rows interlock vertically; only phones keep equal lanes.

rules.name: The Everything Is Visible Rule
rules.body: All links are on the page at rest, unless the viewer folded their group. Groups start open, the filter reaches inside folded ones, and the grid never paginates or scrolls within a group.

rules.name: The Hairline Elevation Rule
rules.body: No surface casts a shadow. If two layers need separating, use a tonal step or a hairline.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Every surface and control the system draws has square corners. Bookmark logos are third-party artwork and keep their own silhouettes.

dos: define every new color as one `light-dark()` pair, and meet WCAG AA in both themes.
use zero radius and a 1px hairline on every new surface and control.
size tiles to their content inside a group, stretching only full rows, and keep equal lanes on phones.
reserve amber for focus, the top match, and selected settings.
use Lucide icons at stroke 1.75 with square caps and miter joins.
give a monogram fallback to anything that loads an external icon.
keep every control at 44px or more on coarse pointers.
match the existing 100ms ease-out for color and background transitions, and honor reduced motion.
donts: add a sidebar, a stat card that is not a link, or a hero header.
round corners on anything the system draws.
add shadows to surfaces. `box-shadow` only draws 1px zero-blur rules and inset rings, and the logo halo is the only blur.
introduce a second typeface or a display or headline size.
use amber for hover, decoration, or emphasis in copy.
tint chrome with a second hue; logos and configured label squares are the only other color.
use tracked uppercase as a decorative line above other text.
